entries.clue: Tolerate leading comedian (5-2)

up = ahead, as in 'two goals up'

annotation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks like a political party to go with left-wing; it is the definition, a social gathering.

entries.clue: A passion about Cambridge University after elevating radio slot? (7)

entries.clue: Deprived, having lost fine headgear (5)

entries.clue: Widely read letter covering military police and love never disappearing from view? (11)

entries.clue: Indication of empty sincerity — politician curtailed vault (7)

indicatorNotes.empty: an empty word has lost its insides, leaving its outer letters

TOMB with its last letter cut

entries.clue: Man bitten by dog? Here’s sign of disease (9)

entries.clue: Understanding English proposal to lead a large system of spies? (9,12)

L = large, as on clothes labels
intelligence = a spy network, as in the intelligence services

entries.clue: 50 per cent unable to read when crossing Channel Islands? That’s wrong (7)

annotation.definitionFit: Hard copy is output on paper, and the phrase for text on paper as opposed to a screen is this one.

entries.clue: Failing to pen a couple of lines working at full capacity (5,3,3)

indicatorNotes.to pen: to pen is to enclose, as in a sheep pen, so A LL goes inside

blocks.note: going out = failing, like a light; it holds ALL

annotation.surface: A struggling writer penning a few lines at full stretch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like writing, which suits 'lines'; here it means to enclose.
annotation.definitionFit: Going all out is making every possible effort, working flat out.

entries.clue: Tackle specialist further down that can accommodate 50 (7)

indicatorNotes.that can accommodate: to accommodate is to house, so the 50 goes inside

blocks.note: sadder = more down, further down in spirits; it holds L

annotation.surface: An expert in football tackles who is more depressed with fifty on board.
annotation.walkthrough: Tackle here is a horse's tack, saddles and bridles, not football or fishing gear.
annotation.definitionFit: A saddler makes and sells saddles and harness, horse tackle.

entries.clue: Echo court imprisoning top inmate? Not any more (7)

indicatorNotes.imprisoning: the court imprisons the top, locking it inside

blocks.note: Echo is E in the NATO alphabet
to see someone is to court them; it holds CAP
a cap is a top, as on a bottle

annotation.surface: A prison court keeping hold of its leading inmate, who then goes missing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Court' is a verb, to woo or see someone, not a court of law.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: someone who has broken out of prison was once an inmate and has stopped being one.

entries.clue: Not musical work involving Poles, such as Perpetuum Mobile? (7)

indicatorNotes.involving: the words wrap round the poles, taking them in

blocks.note: not as printed; it holds NS
N and S, the north and south poles
op. = opus, a numbered musical work

annotation.surface: A remark that a famous perpetual-motion piece is not a musical work with Poles in it.
annotation.walkthrough: A perpetuum mobile is a piece of music played fast without a break, so it is nonstop.
annotation.definitionFit: Perpetuum mobile, perpetual motion, names music that runs without pause: nonstop.
